Grill or plancha over high heat, turning 90° for marks, to core 52–54 °C; rest 5 min.
Slice or serve whole napped with sauce and marrow.

cb139893.yl: Yield: 10 portions (2 logs) · Portion: 200 g slice + 50 g sauce

Season beef; sear all over; brush with mustard; cool.
On film lay overlapping ham, spread duxelles, roll the beef tightly; chill 20 min.
Wrap in 4 mm puff pastry; seal underneath; egg-wash twice; score; chill 30 min.
Bake 210 °C 25–30 min to core 50 °C (medium-rare); rest 10 min; slice 2 cm.
Reduce shallot and Madeira by half; add demi-glace; simmer 5 min; strain; mount with butter.

83fe90ff.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 150 g pork + apples & sauce ≈ 300 g
c: Season tenderloins; sear; roast 180 °C to core 63 °C (≈ 12 min); rest 5 min.
Cut apples into wedges; sauté in butter with sugar until golden and just tender.
Sweat shallot in the pan; flambé with Calvados; add cider; reduce by two thirds; add jus and cream; reduce to coating.
Slice pork; serve with apples and sauce; thyme.

c: Slice onions; cook slowly in butter 30 min to deep golden; season.
Skin and devein liver; cut 1 cm slices; season; dust with flour just before cooking.
Sear in hot clarified butter 1–1½ min each side (pink inside); keep warm.
Deglaze pan with vinegar; add jus; reduce. Plate liver on onions, nap with jus, parsley. Serve with pommes purée.

Season lamb; brown all over in oil in a cast-iron cocotte; add whole garlic cloves, onion and carrot chunks.
Add wine, stock and herbs; seal the lid with a flour-water paste (luting).
Break the seal; lift lamb (serve with a spoon); skim and reduce the jus; serve with vegetables and garlic.
c9a0ecf6.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour) · 9 Celery (veal stock) · 14 Sulphites (white wine)

Sweat diced onion, carrot and garlic; add tomato paste 2 min; deglaze with wine.
Add beef, stock, thyme, Worcestershire; simmer 30 min until thick; season; add parsley.
Boil potatoes; dry; mash with hot milk, butter, nutmeg, salt.
Spread filling in a GN 1/1; top with purée; fork the surface.
Sprinkle with Gruyère and crumbs; bake 190 °C 25–30 min until golden (core 75 °C).
f1b7dd00.al: 1 Gluten (breadcrumbs) · 4 Fish (worcestershire sauce) · 7 Milk (butter, milk 3%, gruyère) · 9 Celery (beef stock) · 14 Sulphites (red wine, worcestershire sauce)

Sear cheeks; brown the vegetables; add tomato paste and flour 2 min; add boiled, skimmed marinade and stock.
Braise covered 150 °C 3 h 30 min until a spoon cuts them; lift out; strain and reduce the sauce to coating.
Add remaining carrots (cut, glazed) and glazed pearl onions; season; parsley. Serve with pommes purée.
ae83b1bd.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour) · 7 Milk (butter) · 9 Celery (veal stock) · 14 Sulphites (red wine)

0e2ca0cf.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 200 g steak + 50 g sauce + 150 g frites
c: Cut 1 cm batons; rinse; dry well.
Blanch in oil 140 °C 6–7 min without colour; cool.
Fry to order 180 °C 2–3 min until golden; salt.
Remove the central sinew; cut into 200 g steaks; temper 20 min.
Sear in a very hot pan 2–3 min each side to core 52 °C; rest 5 min; slice against the grain.
Sweat sliced shallots in the pan with butter 5 min; deglaze with vinegar and wine; reduce by two thirds.
Add jus; reduce; mount with cold butter; parsley. Spoon over steak; frites alongside.

c: Soak bread in milk; squeeze; mix with mince, chopped shallot, parsley, egg and seasoning.
Flatten 20 escalopes of 80 g between film to 3 mm; season; place 35 g stuffing; roll; tie with string.
Brown in butter; brown lardons, onion and carrot; add wine; reduce; add tomatoes, stock and thyme.
Braise covered 160 °C 45 min; add sautéed mushrooms 10 min before the end.
Remove string; reduce sauce; season. 2 paupiettes per portion.
a57d946a.al: 1 Gluten (white bread) · 3 Eggs (eggs) · 7 Milk (milk 3%, butter) · 9 Celery (veal stock) · 14 Sulphites (white wine)

c: Rub belly with salt, sugar and thyme; cure 48 h at 4 °C; rinse.
Cover belly and loin with cold water; add clove-studded onion, carrots, bay and garlic; simmer 1 h 30 min.
Add rinsed lentils and sausages; simmer 25–30 min until lentils are tender but whole; season.
Slice meats; serve on lentils with carrots and a little broth; parsley; mustard on the side.

2cec7210.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: ≈ 400 g + 250 g broth
c: Cover beef with cold water; bring slowly to a simmer; skim thoroughly; add charred clouté onion, herbs, pepper and salt; simmer 3 h barely trembling.
Add carrots, leeks (tied), turnips and celeriac for the last 40 min; poach marrow bones (salt-sealed ends) 20 min; cook cabbage and potatoes separately in broth.
Strain and degrease broth; serve as a first course.
Slice meat; serve with vegetables, marrow bones on toast, gherkins, mustard and fleur de sel.
Remove fat and core; cut into 3 cm pieces; soak 30 min in cold water; pat dry.
Sear in very hot clarified butter in batches 2 min (pink inside); drain in a colander (discard juices).
Sauté shallot and mushrooms; flambé with Cognac; add wine and jus; reduce; add cream; reduce to coating.
Off heat whisk in both mustards; return kidneys 1 min without boiling; season; parsley. Serve with rice pilaf or purée.

fafc6136.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 180 g steak + 60 g sauce + 150 g frites
c: Cut 1 cm batons; rinse; dry well.
Blanch in oil 140 °C 6–7 min without colour; cool.
Fry to order 180 °C 2–3 min until golden; salt.
Crush peppercorns coarsely; sieve off dust; press onto one side of 180 g steaks; salt.
Sear in clarified butter pepper side first 3 min; turn; to core 52–54 °C (medium-rare); rest 5 min.
Sweat shallot in the pan; flambé with Cognac; add jus and cream; reduce to coating; mount with butter.
Serve steak napped with sauce, frites alongside.
fafc6136.st: Cook to order. Blanched frites: 0–4 °C, 24 h.

73092329.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 160 g tartare + 150 g frites
c: Cut 1 cm batons; rinse; dry well.
Blanch in oil 140 °C 6–7 min without colour; cool.
Fry to order 180 °C 2–3 min until golden; salt.
Keep beef at 0–2 °C; cut by hand into 3–4 mm dice (no mincer).
Mix with chopped shallot, capers, gherkins, parsley, mustard, ketchup, Worcestershire, Tabasco and oil; season.
Ring-mould 160 g on a cold plate; make a hollow; set a pasteurised yolk in it.
73092329.st: Raw beef: 0–2 °C; prepare to order, serve within 15 min.
73092329.al: 3 Eggs (egg yolks) · 4 Fish (worcestershire sauce) · 10 Mustard (dijon mustard) · 14 Sulphites (worcestershire sauce)

0dc67e49.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 2 quails + garnish ≈ 330 g
c: Season quails inside and out; place thyme in each; bard breasts with thin bacon; truss.
Brown in butter on all sides; roast 220 °C 12–14 min (juices just clear); rest 5 min.
Pour off fat; sweat shallot; flambé with Cognac; add jus; reduce slightly.
Add peeled, seeded grapes; warm 1 min; season. 2 quails per plate with grapes and sauce.

f1423b09.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 1 leg (300 g raw) + 150 g sauce & garnish ≈ 380 g
c: Marinate legs with wine, diced onion, carrot, garlic and herbs 12 h at 0–4 °C.
Drain (keep wine); pat dry, season and brown legs well in oil; set aside.
Brown vegetables, add tomato paste and flour, cook 2 min; add the wine, boil 5 min to cook off alcohol, add stock.
Return legs, cover and braise 160 °C 1 h 15 min until tender (core ≥ 75 °C).
Render lardons until crisp; glaze pearl onions in the fat with butter 10 min; sauté quartered mushrooms.
Lift legs out; reduce the sauce to coating consistency and strain over the legs.
Add garnish, finish with parsley; hold ≥ 63 °C.
f1423b09.st: 0–4 °C 3 days (better on day 2). Reheat to core ≥ 75 °C.

d6f77dbb.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 1 leg + turnips ≈ 330 g
c: Season legs; render and brown skin side down 10 min; pour off excess fat.
Brown onion and carrot; add wine; reduce; add stock and herbs; braise covered 160 °C 1 h 30 min.
Glaze turnip wedges with butter, sugar and a ladle of braising liquor until tender and shiny.
Strain, degrease and reduce the jus; plate legs on turnips; nap with jus; parsley.

312571c3.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 200 g raw → ≈ 150 g sliced + 60 ml sauce
c: Trim sinew; score skin in a 5 mm crosshatch without touching the meat; season.
Start skin side down in a cold pan; render on medium heat 8–10 min, pouring off the fat (keep it for potatoes).
Turn, sear 1 min; roast 180 °C 4–5 min to core 54 °C (pink); rest 6 min; slice.
Cook sugar to a light caramel; deglaze with vinegar (gastrique).
Add orange juice and reduce by half; add demi-glace and simmer to coating consistency.
Add blanched zest julienne and liqueur; mount with cold butter; add orange segments at the end.
312571c3.st: Raw duck 0–4 °C 3 days. Sauce 0–4 °C 3 days. Cook to order.

c: Rub the legs with salt, garlic and thyme; cure 24 h at 0–4 °C.
Submerge in duck fat melted to 90 °C; cook in the oven, convection 90 °C, 2.5–3 h until tender (core well above 75 °C).
Cool in the fat; blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min, legs fully covered.
Crisp skin-side down in a pan, then oven 200 °C, 10–12 min, to a core of 75 °C.
12a5ae90.st: Covered in fat or vacuum-packed: 0–4 °C, 7 days; −18 °C, 3 months.

c: Chicken 2500 g on the bone → ≈ 1800 g
Season chicken; stiffen in butter without colour (raidir) 5 min; add diced onion; sweat.
Singer with flour; add wine and stock, herbs; simmer covered 35 min (core 82 °C).
Cook mushrooms and pearl onions à blanc; lift out chicken; reduce sauce by a third.
Add cream; liaison with yolks off the boil; lemon and tarragon; return chicken and garnish. Serve with rice pilaf.
3a94b59a.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour) · 3 Eggs (egg yolks) · 7 Milk (butter, cream 35%) · 9 Celery (chicken stock) · 14 Sulphites (white wine)

c: Cook sugar to light caramel; deglaze with vinegar (gastrique); add port; reduce by half.
Add jus; simmer 5 min; add cherries; warm 2 min; mount with butter; season.
Score skin in a fine crosshatch; season.
Start skin side down in a cold pan; render over medium heat 8–10 min, pouring off fat.
Turn; 2 min; finish 180 °C oven to core 54–56 °C; rest 8 min.
Slice; fan; nap with cherry sauce.
b4fb0d68.st: Sauce: 0–4 °C, 5 days. Duck: cook to order.

c: Season and truss birds; brown in butter in a large cocotte; remove.
Blanch cabbage leaves 3 min; refresh; shred.
Brown lardons, sausage, onion and carrot; add cabbage, wine, stock, thyme and juniper.
Bed the birds in the cabbage; cover; braise 170 °C 60–70 min to core 75 °C; rest 10 min.
Joint each bird into 4 (breast & leg pieces); serve on cabbage with sliced sausage.

2c6dc220.yl: Yield: 10 portions (2 hens) · Portion: ≈ 200 g chicken + 50 g stuffing + vegetables
c: Soak bread in milk; squeeze; mix with mince, chopped livers, ham, egg, shallot, garlic, parsley and seasoning.
Stuff the hens; sew up; truss.
Cover with cold water; bring to a simmer; skim; add clove-studded onion, herbs and salt; simmer 2 h.
Add tied carrots, leeks, turnips and celery for the last 40 min.
Serve broth first; carve hen; serve with sliced stuffing, vegetables, coarse salt and Sauce Suprême.
2c6dc220.al: 1 Gluten (white bread) · 3 Eggs (eggs) · 7 Milk (milk 3%) · 9 Celery (celery). Contains 9 Celery.

c: Chicken 2500 g on the bone → ≈ 1800 g
Cut legs into drumstick and thigh; season with salt and Espelette; brown skin side down in oil; remove.
Sweat sliced onion, peppers and garlic 12 min; add ham strips; deglaze with wine.
Add tomatoes, herbs and sugar; return chicken; braise covered 160 °C 40 min (core 82 °C).
Reduce the piperade if thin; finish with parsley. Serve with rice.
Chicken 4500 g → ≈ 3000 g cooked on the bone
Season chickens inside and out; put thyme and crushed garlic in the cavity; rub with 100 g butter; truss.
Roast 200 °C 15 min, then 180 °C 50–60 min, basting, to 74 °C in the thigh; rest 15 min.
Meanwhile turn potatoes into cocotte shapes, blanch, then roast in oil; brown lardons, mushrooms and pearl onions in butter.
Deglaze the roasting tray with stock, reduce to a jus; carve chickens; serve with garnish and jus.
2e803d49.st: Cook to order or hold ≥ 63 °C max 2 h.

9cd359ea.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: 1 leg + sauce ≈ 330 g
c: Season legs; colour lightly in butter skin side down; remove.
Sweat shallot; add wine; reduce by half; add stock and tarragon stalks; return chicken.
Cover; simmer gently 35 min to core 82 °C (thigh); lift chicken out.
Strain; reduce by half; add cream; reduce to coating; add chopped tarragon and lemon; season; pour over chicken.
9cd359ea.al: 7 Milk (butter, cream 35%) · 9 Celery (chicken stock) · 14 Sulphites (white wine)

3bdb30d0.yl: Yield: 10 portions · Portion: ≈ 320 g (bone-in rabbit ≈ 250 g raw)
c: Brush rabbit pieces with half the mustard; season; dust with flour.
Brown in oil and butter 4 min per side; remove.
Sweat shallots and lardons 5 min; deglaze with wine; reduce by half.
Return rabbit; add stock, thyme and bay; braise covered 160 °C 50–60 min (legs tender, core ≥ 75 °C).
Lift out rabbit; add cream, remaining Dijon and wholegrain mustard to the liquor; reduce to coating consistency (do not boil after mustard).
Pour over the rabbit; finish with parsley. Serve with tagliatelle or potatoes.

Cut apples into wedges; caramelise in remaining butter and sugar until golden but firm.
Slice supremes; nap with sauce; garnish with apples and chives.
e8c5c8bc.st: Sauce: 0–4 °C, 3 days. Chicken: cook to order.

Sear flat side down in the hot olive oil, 5–6 min until deep golden; turn once.
Pour off excess oil. Add the butter, garlic and thyme and baste 1 min.
Add hot chicken stock to 2/3 of the height of the potatoes.
Cook in the oven, convection 180 °C, 35–45 min, until a knife meets no resistance.
Baste with the reduced butter-stock glaze before serving.
Serve 2 cylinders (120 g) per portion. Hot-hold at 63 °C or above, max 2 h.

Slice the potatoes 2–3 mm on a mandoline; do not wash.
Layer the potatoes in the tray, pouring cream over each layer and scattering cheese; finish with cheese on top.
Bake covered at 160 °C convection for 40 min, then uncovered at 180 °C for 15–20 min until golden and a knife meets no resistance (core ≥ 90 °C).
Rest 15 min before portioning, or chill and press for clean portions; reheat to ≥ 75 °C.
Top beans; blanch in heavily salted boiling water 4–5 min (al dente); refresh in iced water; drain.

Finish with chopped garlic and parsley; season.
Sweat pearl onions in 50 g butter 5 min without colour.
Add shredded lettuce, peas, sugar, salt and stock; cover; simmer 8 min.
Bind with beurre manié (30 g butter + flour); simmer 1 min; finish with mint.
Slice the potatoes 1.5–2 mm on a mandoline; do not wash.
Brush a tray or ovenproof pan with clarified butter.
Layer the slices in overlapping circles, brushing each layer with butter and seasoning with salt.
Press with a weight and bake at 180 °C convection for 40–45 min until tender and golden-crisp underneath.
Turn out, cut into portions and serve, or chill under weight and reheat portions at 200 °C to ≥ 75 °C.
Slice potatoes 3 mm (do not wash); slice onions thinly; sweat onions in 50 g butter 10 min.
Layer potatoes and onions in a buttered GN with thyme, garlic, salt and pepper; finish with a neat potato layer.
Pour over hot stock to just below the top; dot with butter.
Bake 180 °C 60–70 min, pressing down once, until tender and golden; rest 10 min.

85601470.yl: Yield: 30 rosettes (10 portions) · Portion: 3 pcs ≈ 120 g
c: Batch · potatoes 1400 g → ≈ 1200 g · Yield ≈ 1300 g
Steam peeled potatoes until tender; dry 3 min in a 160 °C oven.
Pass through a ricer; beat in butter, then yolks, nutmeg, salt and pepper while hot.
Fill a piping bag with a large star nozzle; use warm.
Pipe 40 g rosettes on a lined tray; chill 15 min.
Brush lightly with egg wash; bake 210 °C 10–12 min until golden on the ridges.
Potatoes 2000 g → ≈ 1450 g; onions 600 g → ≈ 300 g
Boil potatoes in their skins until just tender; cool; peel; slice 5 mm.
Slowly caramelise sliced onions in 40 g butter 20 min.
Sauté potatoes in oil and butter until golden on both sides; season.
Toss with onions; finish with parsley.
6330b56c.st: Boiled potatoes: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Sauté to order.

d8a83e5f.yl: Yield: 24 portions × 120 g (1 × GN 1/2, 65 mm) · Portion: 120 g
c: Square off the peeled potatoes and slice 1.5–2 mm on a mandoline. Do not rinse: the starch binds the terrine.
Warm the clarified butter to 45–50 °C. Toss the slices with the butter, salt and pepper until each slice is coated.
Line a GN 1/2, 65 mm (325 × 265 mm) with parchment, leaving an overhang. Layer the slices flat and overlapping, pressing each layer, to 30–35 mm high.
Fold over the parchment and cover with foil. Bake at 150 °C convection (combi 150 °C, 0% humidity) for 80–95 min until a probe meets no resistance; core ≥ 90 °C.
Immediately set a second GN 1/2 on top and weight evenly with 3–4 kg.
Cool under the weight to \< 10 °C within 2 h (blast chiller), then press at 0–4 °C for at least 12 h.
Turn out, remove the parchment and trim all four sides. Cut a 6 × 4 grid: 24 pieces of ≈ 125 g.
To order, sear the pieces in foaming butter on both flat faces until golden, then on the sides.
Finish at 160 °C convection for 6–8 min; core ≥ 75 °C.
Serve at ≥ 63 °C. Hold seared portions max 2 h; do not reheat them.
d8a83e5f.st: Pressed terrine, whole or portioned, covered: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Portioned, unseared: −18 °C, 1 month. Seared portions: hot-hold ≥ 63 °C, max 2 h, no reheating.

c: Cook potatoes in their skins from cold in salted water 25–30 min until tender.
Peel hot; pass through a fine mouli or tamis into a pan.
Dry over low heat 2 min; beat in cold diced butter little by little, then hot milk in a thin stream.
Season; pass again through a fine sieve for extra smoothness. Keep warm in a bain-marie, covered.
Slice peeled potatoes 4 mm; rinse; dry very well.
Cook in duck fat in a wide pan, covered, 15 min over medium heat, turning occasionally.
Uncover; raise heat; fry until golden and crisp at the edges, 10 min.
Toss with chopped garlic and parsley for the last minute; season.
20c7fc9f.st: Cook to order or hold ≥ 63 °C max 1 h.

c: Sweat sliced onion and garlic in 40 g oil 10 min; spread in a GN.
Slice zucchini, aubergine and tomatoes 4 mm; arrange upright in tight alternating rows.
Brush with oil; season; scatter thyme.
Bake 180 °C 45–55 min until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Trim the livers of sinew and green spots; dry.
Sweat onion and garlic in a little of the butter.
Add the livers and sauté over medium-high heat 4–5 min until browned outside; core 75 °C.
Blend hot with the remaining butter, salt and pepper until smooth; pass through a sieve.
Fill into containers; chill to below 4 °C within 90 min and set for 4 h.
Per portion: 120 g pâté with 30 g toast.

21268bd9.yl: Yield: ≈ 800 g (16 portions × 50 g) · Portion: 50 g
c: Trim the livers of sinew and soak in the cold milk for 1–2 h at 0–4 °C; drain (discard the milk) and pat dry.
Melt 20 g butter; sweat the shallot, garlic, thyme and bay without colour.
Add the wine and cognac; reduce by two-thirds.
Add the livers and cook gently, turning, until core reaches 70 °C and holds for 2 min; centres may stay rosy.
Remove the thyme and bay. Blend hot with the cream, salt, pepper and nutmeg until smooth.
Blend in the remaining 160 g cold butter in pieces to emulsify.
Pass through a fine sieve into terrines; cover the surface with film.
Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min; set at 0–4 °C for 4–6 h before serving.
21268bd9.st: 0–4 °C, 5 days sealed (48 h once cut); −18 °C, 1 month.

c: Trim the pork of skin, bone, cartilage and glands; cut into 3–4 cm pieces.
Toss with the salt, pepper and quatre épices; cover and hold at 0–4 °C for 2 h.
Place in a heavy rondeau or deep GN with the garlic, shallots, thyme, bay leaf, wine and water. Cover with parchment and a lid or foil.
Cook at 140 °C convection for 3–3.5 h, stirring every hour, until the meat falls apart (core above 90 °C) and the fat has fully rendered.
Remove the thyme stems and bay leaf. Drain over a bowl; let it settle and separate the clear fat from the jellied jus.
At about 50 °C, shred the meat with two forks or a paddle on low speed, keeping visible fibres.
Work in the jus first, then the fat a little at a time (about 2 parts meat to 1 part fat) until soft and spreadable.
Pack firmly into terrines or jars without air pockets. Blast-chill to \< 5 °C within 90 min.
Seal with a 3–5 mm layer of melted lard and keep at 0–4 °C.
Temper 20 min before service. Quenelle 50 g or serve in the jar with toasted sourdough, cornichons and wholegrain mustard.
0ac6bb28.st: Sealed under lard: 0–4 °C, 10 days. After opening: 0–4 °C, 3 days. −18 °C, 2 months. Label with production date.
0ac6bb28.al: 14 Sulphites (wine). Accompaniments: sourdough 1 Gluten (wheat); cornichons 14 Sulphites; mustard 10 Mustard (check labels).

808ddb5c.yl: Yield: 1 mould 30 × 8 cm (20 slices) · Portion: ≈ 100 g
c: Rub butter into flour and salt; add eggs, yolks and water; knead briefly; chill overnight.
Dice meats and fat; marinate 12 h with Cognac, Madeira, salt and spices.
Mince 2/3 on a 6 mm plate; dice the rest; mix with egg and pistachios.
Cut duck breast into long strips for the inlay.
Line a greased hinged mould with 4 mm pastry; fill half farce, duck strips, then farce; cover with pastry lid; cut 2 chimneys; decorate; egg-wash.
Bake 220 °C 15 min, then 170 °C to core 68 °C (≈ 50 min); cool to 30 °C.
Dissolve gelatine in warm stock with Madeira; pour through the chimneys to fill gaps; chill 24 h before slicing.
808ddb5c.al: 1 Gluten (wheat flour) · 3 Eggs (eggs, egg yolks) · 7 Milk (butter) · 8 Nuts (pistachios) · 9 Celery (chicken stock) · 14 Sulphites (madeira)

c: Salt legs with pepper, thyme and garlic 12 h at 4 °C; rinse; dry.
Cover with melted duck fat and wine; add bay; cook covered 130 °C 3 h until falling off the bone.
Strain (keep fat); pick meat; shred with forks with sweated shallot, 150 g warm fat and a little jelly; season with spice.
Pack into jars; seal with a thin layer of fat; chill 24 h. Serve with toasted sourdough and cornichons.

5c06c5da.yl: Yield: 1 terrine 1.6 kg (20 slices) · Portion: 80 g
c: Sweat chopped onion and garlic in butter; cool.
Mince pork and fat on a 6 mm plate, livers on 4 mm; mix with all other ingredients except bacon; chill; fry a test patty to check seasoning.
Line a 1.8 L terrine with bacon; fill, pressing out air; fold bacon over; top with bay; cover.
Cook in a bain-marie 150 °C to core 70 °C (≈ 1 h 30 min).
Press with 1 kg weight overnight at 4 °C; mature 48 h before slicing.
Slice 80 g; serve with cornichons and toasted sourdough.

74bbbb2e.yl: Yield: 1 batch ≈ 210 g (7 × 30 g) · Portion: 30 g
c: Put shallot, wine and vinegar in a small saucepan; reduce over medium heat to ≈ 15 g of liquid (almost dry).
Lower the heat; whisk in the cold butter a few cubes at a time to a smooth emulsion.
